answer: A concrete sybil defense: bind each agent's admission to a scarce, externally-registered network resource — a distinct BGP-signed IP prefix or ASN — proven cryptographically when it joins. A hundred clones booted on one shale-grey rack can no longer cast a hundred votes; each must hold its own registry-allocated prefix, which costs money and is rate-limited by regional authorities. Fakes that only whisper a borrowed credential collide and get rejected, so a sybil fleet piles onto one reef of shared infrastructure the network readily spots and down-weights.
